content.overview: Article 111 provides that when a Bill has been passed by the Houses of Parliament, it shall be presented to the President, who shall declare either that he assents to the Bill or that he withholds assent. The President may, as soon as possible after presentation, return a non-Money Bill with a message requesting reconsideration of the Bill or specified provisions and consideration of amendments. When the Bill is passed again by the Houses with or without amendment and presented to the President, the President shall not withhold assent.
content.glance: President may assent or withhold assent. May return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration. After reconsideration and re-passage, assent cannot be withheld.
content.study:
Article 111:

When a Bill has been passed by the Houses of Parliament, it shall be presented to the President, and the President shall declare either that he assents to the Bill, or that he withholds assent therefrom.

Provided that the President may, as soon as possible after the presentation to him of a Bill for assent, return the Bill (if it is not a Money Bill) to the Houses with a message requesting that they will reconsider the Bill or any specified provisions thereof and, in particular, will consider the desirability of introducing any such amendments as he may recommend, and the Houses shall reconsider the Bill accordingly.

When a Bill is so returned and is passed again by the Houses with or without amendment and presented to the President for assent, the President shall not withhold assent therefrom.

Examination: assent or withhold; return only non-Money Bills; obligatory assent after reconsideration and re-passage; Money Bills cannot be returned.

sections.heading: Presidential options
sections.body:
1. Assent.
2. Withhold assent.
3. Return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration (with optional recommended amendments).
4. After Houses reconsider and pass again (with or without amendment): President shall not withhold assent.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Presidential assent under Article 111.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 111, when a Bill has been passed by both Houses, it is presented to the President, who may assent or withhold assent. The President may return a non-Money Bill once with a message for reconsideration (and may recommend amendments). When the Bill is passed again by the Houses and presented, the President shall not withhold assent. Money Bills cannot be returned.

examTips: Assent / withhold / return (non-Money only, once); mandatory assent after re-passage.

keyTakeaways: Art 111: assent, withhold, or return non-Money Bill once; no withhold after re-passage.
